variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: A vector database stores records alongside numeric embeddings and retrieves records whose vectors are near a query vector. The embedding represents learned features; the database owns identity, metadata, indexing, filtering, updates, replication, and the query contract around those numbers.
variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Cosine similarity
pairs.detail: Compares vector direction after accounting for magnitude.
pairs.explanation: Compares vector direction after accounting for magnitude. If vectors are normalized to unit length, cosine ranking and inner-product ranking are closely related.

pairs.label: Inner product
pairs.explanation: Rewards alignment and vector magnitude. Use it when the embedding model was trained and evaluated for dot-product retrieval.

pairs.label: Euclidean distance
pairs.explanation: Ranks points by straight-line distance. Its scale depends directly on preprocessing and the geometry produced by the embedding model.

variants.hint:
Cosine similarity: Compares vector direction after accounting for magnitude.

Inner product: Rewards alignment and vector magnitude.

Euclidean distance: Ranks points by straight-line distance.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Keeping these boundaries clear helps you find the place to change when the system behaves unexpectedly.

variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Exact flat search
pairs.explanation: Scores every eligible vector. It provides exact top-k references and can be practical for small collections, highly selective pre-filters, or accelerated batch evaluation.

pairs.label: HNSW graph
pairs.explanation: Traverses a multilayer proximity graph. Build connectivity affects memory and indexing cost; query-time search effort controls the recall-latency operating point.

pairs.label: IVF and product quantization
pairs.detail: Probes selected partitions and can score compressed codes before exact reranking.
pairs.explanation: Probes selected partitions and can score compressed codes before exact reranking. Training data, probes, code size, and rerank depth shape quality.

pairs.label: Disk-oriented graph search
pairs.detail: Keeps a compact routing structure in memory and reads candidate neighborhoods from SSD.
pairs.explanation: Keeps a compact routing structure in memory and reads candidate neighborhoods from SSD. Storage layout and IO behavior become part of the latency model.

HNSW graph: Traverses a multilayer proximity graph.

IVF and product quantization: Probes selected partitions and can score compressed codes before exact reranking.

Disk-oriented graph search: Keeps a compact routing structure in memory and reads candidate neighborhoods from SSD.

pairs.label: Create the representation
pairs.detail: Run the versioned chunker and embedding model.
pairs.explanation: Run the versioned chunker and embedding model. Validate dimensions, finite values, normalization, and payload size.

pairs.label: Commit a versioned mutation

variants.prompt: Why should an ANN index be evaluated against exact nearest-neighbor results on representative queries?

Exact search always has lower latency than ANN search

variants.prompt: How do stable point IDs, source versions, and tombstones work together during retries?
options: They deduplicate delivery, reject older mutations, and prevent deleted content from being resurrected
They make every ANN result exact
They remove the need for backups
